_note: Two asset universes. The universe a portfolio belongs to decides which benchmark index beta is estimated against, which crisis magnitudes are meaningful for its holdings, and which risk-free rate is the right one to subtract. Applying an S&P 500 drawdown to an NSE portfolio is a category error; the universe is what prevents it.

NSE_INDIA.label: NSE India (NIFTY 50 constituents)
NSE_INDIA.trading_days_note: NSE settles roughly 246-250 sessions a year after weekends and exchange holidays. Using 252 here instead moves an annualised volatility by ~0.4%, which is immaterial next to estimation error - but the number is declared rather than assumed.
NSE_INDIA.risk_free_basis: Indicative 91-day Government of India T-bill yield

US.label: US large cap (S&P 500 constituents)
US.trading_days_note: 252 is the conventional US count and the one every published Sharpe figure you will be compared against uses.
